subject: Physics
subtopic: Two-dimensional constant acceleration and projectile model
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; this matrix is an owner-approved question-demand extension and does not alter the ordinary Standard Grade-9 Motion matrix.

must_contain: One declared x-y frame, origin and time origin for the whole event.
The same elapsed time on both component descriptions.
Recombination only from components evaluated at the same instant.

controlled_variation.vary: whether only x, only y, or both component velocities change
controlled_variation.hold: one common frame, sign convention and elapsed time
controlled_variation.notice: component histories may differ while still describing one object

controlled_variation.vary: the observation time at which the state is requested
controlled_variation.hold: the same component functions and frame
controlled_variation.notice: x(t) and y(t) must be evaluated at the same t before they can form one plane state

must_contain: A separate validity check that a_x and a_y are each constant over the interval on which their equations are used.
Separate x and y constant-acceleration equations with signed component values.
Any event time found from one axis reused on the other axis for that same event.

controlled_variation.hold: initial component velocities, frame and common time
controlled_variation.notice: each axis responds only to its own acceleration component

controlled_variation.vary: one acceleration component from constant to time-varying
controlled_variation.hold: the other axis model and the same physical interval
controlled_variation.notice: constant-acceleration validity is checked per component rather than granted to the whole problem at once

controlled_variation.vary: which axis supplies the event condition used to find time
controlled_variation.hold: one event and one physical clock
controlled_variation.notice: the event time obtained from either axis must be used on both axes

must_contain: A post-release force/model statement before projectile equations.
a_x=0 and a_y=-g under an explicit +y-up convention.
Horizontal and oblique launch treated as initial-condition variations.
An explicit event condition before solving apex, same-height return or unequal-height landing.
At the apex only v_y is zero; horizontal velocity and downward acceleration remain.
Same-height shortcuts used only when launch and landing heights are equal.
For horizontal or unequal-height launch, flight time is obtained from vertical motion and then shared with horizontal motion.
A requested speed/direction/position/range result reconstructed from simultaneous components rather than memorized in isolation.

controlled_variation.vary: initial vertical component from zero to positive
controlled_variation.notice: horizontal and oblique launch use the same component laws with different initial conditions

controlled_variation.vary: the requested event among a later time, apex, same-height return and lower landing
controlled_variation.hold: the same projectile model and one shared clock
controlled_variation.notice: different events are identified by different vertical component conditions before time is solved

controlled_variation.vary: landing height from equal to launch height to below launch height
controlled_variation.hold: u_x, u_y and gravity-only free flight
controlled_variation.notice: same-height shortcuts stop being valid when Delta y at landing is not zero

controlled_variation.vary: the requested output among velocity vector, speed, direction, height, range or flight time
controlled_variation.hold: the same event time and component state
controlled_variation.notice: the output is reconstructed from one component model rather than selected from a catalogue of separate projectile laws

family.invariant_demand: Declare one frame and clock, represent the motion with simultaneous signed components, validate the component kinematic model, and for projectile questions choose both the gravity-only specialization and the event condition before reconstructing the requested result.
family.difficult_move: Keeping model choice and event choice separate: first decide which component equations are valid, then decide what condition identifies the requested instant, while preserving one common clock.
family.independent_check: Signs/units and one-clock consistency must hold; projectile states must preserve a_x=0 and a_y=-g, apex must keep nonzero downward acceleration, and same-height shortcuts must be rejected when landing height differs.

support_ladder.handed_over: Frame, component table, constant-acceleration status and projectile assumptions are labelled.
Frame and known component values are labelled; learner selects component equations/model.
Only the physical story and requested output are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: A plane-motion story must first be converted into signed x/y component states before equations are selected.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the component representation and common-time structure

transfer.changed_demand: Acceleration is given as a vector and the learner must decide whether constant-acceleration equations may be used on each component.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that model validity is checked component-wise

transfer.changed_demand: A launched object is still under propulsion or has important drag, so the standard projectile specialization may not apply.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether gravity-only free flight is a valid model

transfer.changed_demand: The question asks for range, height, flight time or later velocity without naming the intermediate component equations.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which component condition defines the requested event
